subject: Predicting mean values on grid/holding out data to determine model fit

messages.author: 22dc0d80dd88c700
messages.subject: Predicting mean values on grid/holding out data to determine model fit
parts:
I'm working on an INLA analysis in which I'm trying to determine which environmental variables best predict timing of breeding (day of year) in a falcon species. I found that my best model included a fixed effect of start-of-spring index (day of year that leaf out occurs) and a spatial random effect. I'm interested in eventually using the model to predict laydates across my study area. I've tried to follow a few tutorials to predict the posterior mean and SD onto a map, but I'm having some trouble getting my model to do that. I've included my code and data here that gets me right up to that point. 

Right now I'm trying to follow this example, but I'm not sure how to alter my code to do it: https://www.stat.washington.edu/peter/591/INLA.html

I was also wondering about determining model fit by holding out a subset of the data. Would it be reasonable to make predictions with the model (map estimated laydate across my study area) and use something like RMSE to see how well the model values match the actual withheld laydates?

My predictor variable (start-of-spring index) is available as a raster layer across my study area. Could I use that for prediction instead of using inla.mesh.projector?

Thanks,

Jay

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Predicting mean values on grid/holding out data to determine model fit
parts:
Hi,
You’d need to to project/evaluate the field on the mesh at some point, but there are several options for how/when/where to do that. I see you’re already using inlabru for some plotting; you might consider using it for the estimation as well, as it should make the posterior prediction a lot easier and flexible; you may need to convert the raster to SpatialPixelsDataFrame, but see the tutorial examples on inlabru.org for how to do that and setup such a model and do prediction.
(In the development version of inlabru one can actually use predict() on regular inla() output, but the raster/SpatialPixels handling I think requires setting up the model in inlabru format)

Finn
